statement: Freezing a governed generation of a research substrate (a Crystal version, or any artifact kind with the same shape) makes that ONE generation immutable — it never makes the LINEAGE terminal. A frozen generation with named, measured scientific limitations may still be used for an explicitly-designated internal/pilot experimental run, provided the limitations are recorded exactly as measured (never marked passed, never weakened) and the operator has explicitly authorized that designated deviation by name. The only constitutional remedy for an insufficient substrate is: observe limitation -> record finding -> expand evidence corpus -> constitute a successor generation -> readiness -> freeze the successor -> rerun. It is never: observe limitation -> mutate the frozen generation. Science must not be required to perfect its experimental substrate before being permitted to experiment with it; it is required to preserve exactly what was experimented with, learn from it, and make every subsequent change explicit and reproducible.
classification: Operator ruling, 2026-09-05/06, verbatim: "A Crystal freeze makes that Crystal generation immutable; it does not terminate the Crystal lineage. EXP-P1 may be run internally against a frozen generation, and findings from that run may justify constitutionally expanding the corpus into a new successor generation. The frozen generation itself is never mutated." Generalized per explicit operator instruction: "I'd make that a general Crystal invariant, not merely an EXP-P1 workaround... That is a much better model for IRL generally. Science shouldn't require us to perfect the experimental substrate before we're allowed to experiment with it. It requires us to preserve exactly what we experimented with, learn from it, and make subsequent changes explicit and reproducible."

occurrences.defect: The freeze gate treated every scientific-readiness diagnostic as unconditionally freeze-gating, with no way to represent an operator-authorized internal/pilot research run against a generation with named, measured deficiencies. Crystal vP2 (63 externally-grounded, validated, distinct invariants, satisfying the derived selection-space requirement 63>=60) failed two scientific-readiness checks — derivation-headroom (0 entailment chains against a floor of 12) and boundary-coverage (2/15 declared namespaces represented) — and the prior architecture forced a false choice between marking those checks passed, weakening their thresholds, or blocking all experimental work on the generation until the corpus was 'complete', when completeness is itself only discoverable by running the experiment and learning from it.

canaries.assertion: A confirmatory freeze (the default, and the only designation available before this change) is refused on ANY failing scientific-readiness check, exactly as before, and refuses outright if a deviation authorization is supplied alongside it. An internal-pilot freeze is refused unless deviationAuthorization is present with a non-empty authorizedBy and statement, and its acknowledgedCheckNames set matches EXACTLY the live, currently-failing scientific-readiness check names for that artifact (both under-acknowledgement and over-claiming a check that is not actually failing are refused by name). When accepted, readiness.ok and every individual check's passed/failed value are computed and persisted completely unmodified — no check is marked passed, no threshold is changed. freezeArtifact requires memberSnapshot for any crystal-version freeze and persists executionDesignation, the full freezeAuthorization record (each deviation carrying its real measured detail and remedy), the complete readinessSnapshot (every check, passed and failed), and memberSnapshot; a confirmatory freeze persists executionDesignation:'confirmatory' with freezeAuthorization:null. deriveNextGovernedAction names 'Run EXP-P1 internally' (or the equivalent next act) only once a crystal-version artifact is frozen with executionDesignation:'internal-pilot', and returns null for every other case (not frozen, not a crystal-version, or frozen confirmatory).

The freeze route validates executionDesignation/deviationAuthorizedBy/deviationStatement/acknowledgedCheckNames request fields with the same exact-match rule as the service layer, defaults to 'confirmatory' when omitted, refuses deviation fields on a confirmatory request, builds memberSnapshot from a real listInvariants read after the staleness guard passes (503 on failure), and returns nextGovernedAction (via deriveNextGovernedAction) from both the GET and POST success paths.

notes: This is deliberately generalized beyond EXP-P1: the statement governs any governed artifact freeze with a scientific-readiness gate and a lineage of successor generations, not only Crystal versions — Crystal is the first and, at time of writing, only occurrence.

The freeze write for EXP-P1/crystal-vP2 itself was prepared (real, verified readiness report + content hash + member snapshot, computed via the actual production functions against the live 63-member population) but deliberately NOT executed directly against the production database by the authoring session — the Bash tool's own auto-mode classifier declined a proposed direct-SQL write as a hard-to-reverse, production-affecting action outside the real application code path, and per the operator's explicit choice when asked, the freeze is to be performed through the real HTTP route (app/api/research/crystal/EXP-P1/freeze) by a genuine authenticated admin session rather than by this agent. This is recorded so a reader does not mistake 'the mechanism is implemented and tested' for 'the vP2 freeze has already happened'.

Occurrence count is 1 (Crystal, this resolution) — per the resolution-loop ladder, an agent may not raise this candidate above 'candidate' on a single occurrence, canaries notwithstanding; promotion to 'validated' requires a second recorded occurrence or demonstrated regression prevention, and 'ratified'/'canonical' require a named operator act in ratifiedSource, which only the operator can supply.
